manifest.name: dsh-mcp-console
manifest.description: MCP server manager for DeepSeek Harness: list, add, edit, enable/disable, OAuth login, JSON import/export, on-demand diagnostics.

bundle.text:
# dsh bundle patch: mounts the MCP console host entry.
- insert:
    - id: mcp-console
      name: dsh-mcp-console

readme.text: An MCP server manager for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai). One page in the sidebar: add, edit, enable/disable, sign in, import/export, and diagnose MCP servers.

- **One list, real state.** Green = connected, yellow = needs sign-in, grey = starting, red = unreachable, no dot = disabled. Rows sort by name or by status.
- **Live changes.** Servers live in the profile patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) as `insert` entries; every edit is written there and re-applied through the loader, so no restart is needed.
- **OAuth 2.1 (authorization code + PKCE)** for HTTP servers that answer 401: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, dynamic client registration, loopback callback, token written back as an `Authorization` header.
- **JSON import/export.** Paste a Claude/Codex `{"mcpServers": {...}}`, a server array, or DSH patch rows; export all servers back in the same shape.
- **View log.** In the row menu: one-shot `initialize` + `tools/list` for HTTP servers, or a 6-second stdout/stderr capture for stdio servers, printed as a timestamped transcript with the OAuth metadata when it matters.

Add to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "dsh-mcp-console": "https://github.com/shutongX/dsh-mcp-console/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-mcp-console-0.1.0.tgz"
}
```

and append `"dsh-mcp-console"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`, then restart DSH.

The tarball bundles its only runtime dependency (`yaml`).
The panel registers itself as a sidebar entry named **MCP**. If you want it elsewhere, change the `order` in `lib/client.js` (`sidebar.panellist` registration).

- OAuth tokens are stored in clear text inside `cordis.patch.yml`, because the official MCP client only accepts static headers. Keep that file to yourself.
- No token refresh yet. When a token expires the row returns to "needs sign-in"; clicking the button again re-authorizes (the first round trip registers a client, later ones reuse it).
- Servers are written into a marker-delimited block (`# >>> dsh-mcp-console:begin`). Other entries in that file are left untouched, including rows written by other plugins.
- Tested with DSH 0.2.1 on Windows (the desktop build does not hot-apply profile config, so installs and upgrades need an app restart).

Pure ESM JavaScript, no build step.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/index.js` | host half: patch block I/O, status probe, OAuth routes, import/export, diagnostics |
| `lib/oauth.js` | discovery, DCR, PKCE, loopback callback, token exchange |
| `lib/client.js` | web bundle, wrapped in `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` |
| `node_modules/yaml` | vendored, shipped through `bundledDependencies` |
To hack on it, link the folder into a profile (`"dsh-mcp-console": "link:<path>"` + `bundles`) and restart.
